name: printing-press-amend
conclusion_quantitative: printing-press-amend (Ask) specifies 5 of 5 categories: 8 autonomy limits, 8 clarification rules, 10+ approval gates, 10+ validation rules, 5 escalation rules. Strongest: approval gates.
conclusion_qualitative: printing-press-amend turns friction from a dogfooding session, or asks the user types directly, into a pull request that amends a published CLI in the public library. The user stays in the loop at two checkpoints, scope after capture and the pull-request draft before opening, and is asked whenever inputs are ambiguous or a finding needs a judgment call. Between checkpoints the agent works unattended within set limits, validating its fixes, patch records and documentation. It stops and reports to the user on outdated binaries, repeated validation failures or personal data found in the code.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_quantitative: 8 autonomy limits (8 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly prose.
autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: There are 8 rules, all strict, 1 tied to a situation, mostly running text. The front matter limits the agent to `Bash`, `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Glob`, `Grep` and `AskUserQuestion`. It must not amend or regenerate on a binary below the required version floor, runs the sniff step only when the user asked for it, and keeps all edits inside the CLI's folder in the managed clone. Between the two user checkpoints it plans, fixes and validates unattended, and after the final checkpoint it pushes and opens the pull request on its own.

clarification_rules.conclusion_quantitative: 8 clarification rules (7 mandatory, 1 advisory; 3 conditional), mostly list.
clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: There are 8 rules, 7 strict and 1 counted as a suggestion (it contains "should"), 3 tied to a situation, mostly bullet points. The agent asks the user when the input mode is ambiguous, when no target CLI is named, when asks span several CLIs or use vague verbs, and when the sniff target URL is missing. It asks whether to skip findings that may duplicate existing pull requests, whether a machine-level fix should be deferred, and whether unknown proper nouns should be scrubbed as personal data.

validation.conclusion_quantitative: 10+ validation rules (10 mandatory, 0 advisory; 4 conditional), mostly prose.
validation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 10 or more rules (the first 10 are kept), all strict, 4 tied to a situation, mostly running text. After editing, the agent runs the consolidated validator and retries targeted fixes up to 3 times. It checks that at least one patch file was recorded and that every user-facing change ships matching, accurate documentation verified by the skill verifier, blocking the pull-request draft until that checklist is empty. It also scans the Go source for personal data from the stop-list.

escalation.conclusion_quantitative: 5 escalation rules (5 mandatory, 0 advisory; 4 conditional), mostly prose.
escalation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 5 rules, all strict, 4 tied to a situation, all in running text. The agent stops and tells the user when the binary is older than the minimum or the upgrade fails, and aborts when the dogfooded binary is older than the published one. After 3 failed validation rounds it shows the final error log and does not open the pull request, and personal data found in Go source blocks the run until the user resolves it.
